name: Marriott International, Inc.
executive_summary:
Marriott International is the world’s largest hotel franchisor and manager, operating an asset-light model with more than 10,000 properties and roughly 1.8 million rooms globally. The quantitative screen rates MAR a buy, driven by quality and growth-at-a-reasonable-price signals (Neff PEGY, Piotroski F-Score 7/9, earnings quality, dividend growth, Magic Formula) rather than classic deep-value metrics. FY2025 earnings strengthened (pretax income $3.39bn per the 10-K; net income $2.60bn per Yahoo fallback), and H1 2026 fee revenue and RevPAR trends remain positive, though Q2 net income softened on litigation and Middle East weakness. The central debate is whether a premium franchise with fee-based compounding justifies a ~37x P/E and elevated leverage funded partly by debt and aggressive buybacks, against a cyclical travel backdrop and unresolved Starwood litigation exposure.

---
investment_thesis:
For a value-oriented investor, MAR is a **quality compounder at a full price**, not a statistically cheap stock. The screen’s buy signal rests on five distinct factor families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—passing simultaneously with high data quality (18/20 metrics). The Neff PEGY pass (PEGY 0.43 on ~4.3% earnings growth) and Piotroski score of 7 reflect improving profitability, positive operating cash flow exceeding net income, and no share dilution, consistent with a durable fee engine.

Business quality is strong. At 30 June 2026, Marriott reported 10,082 properties and 1,813,698 rooms (10-Q, filed 3 Aug 2026), with a development pipeline of nearly 4,200 properties and ~629,000 rooms. H1 2026 net fee revenues rose 12% year-on-year to $2,945m, led by franchise fees (+18% to $1,895m), while worldwide RevPAR increased 3.8% (ADR-led). The model converts earnings to cash: FY2025 operating cash flow was $3.21bn and free cash flow $2.61bn (Yahoo fallback; filing bodies lack full cash-flow statements).

What the screen **does not** capture is headline valuation stretch. MAR fails 17 of 22 models, including Graham Defensive/Enterprising, deep value, FCF yield (<5%), acquirer’s multiple, and financial health (high debt-to-equity, current ratio 0.43, negative book equity). The buy case therefore hinges on **franchise economics and earnings durability** outweighing balance-sheet optics distorted by decades of repurchases ($3.3bn in FY2025; $1.82bn in H1 2026 per Q2 2026 10-Q). For a value investor willing to pay for quality, the screen’s quality/GARP/risk cluster offers a disciplined entry framework; for strict deep-value mandates, the same data argues caution.

financial_review:
### Annual results (10-K)

Two annual 10-K filings are indexed (FY2024 filed 11 Feb 2025; FY2025 filed 10 Feb 2026), both with body extracts. **Income-statement tables are truncated in the extracts**; pretax income and geographic revenue disclosures are available from filings; remaining P&L and balance-sheet line items below use **Yahoo `financials_annual.json` with explicit fallback**.

| Metric | FY2025 (10-K / fallback) | FY2024 (10-K / fallback) | FY2023 (Yahoo fallback) |
|--------|--------------------------|--------------------------|-------------------------|
| Pretax income | **$3,394m** (10-K) | **$3,151m** (10-K) | $3,378m (Yahoo) |
| Total revenue | $26,186m (Yahoo) | $25,100m (Yahoo) | $23,713m (Yahoo) |
| Net income | $2,601m (Yahoo) | $2,375m (Yahoo) | $3,083m (Yahoo) |
| Diluted EPS | $9.51 (Yahoo) | $8.33 (Yahoo) | $10.18 (Yahoo) |
| Operating income | $4,139m (Yahoo) | $3,844m (Yahoo) | $3,924m (Yahoo) |

FY2025 pretax income rose 7.7% versus FY2024 ($3,394m vs $3,151m, 10-K). Net income and EPS also advanced on the Yahoo series (+9.5% and +14% respectively), though FY2023 net income was elevated by a lower effective tax rate and is not the appropriate base for normalised growth. International revenue (including cost reimbursements) was $5,672m in 2025 vs $5,512m in 2024 (10-K geographic note).

**Balance sheet (FY2025, Yahoo fallback):** total assets $27.5bn; total debt $17.1bn; net debt $15.8bn; cash $358m; stockholders’ equity **−$3.8bn** (treasury stock $27.9bn); working capital −$4.8bn; current ratio 0.43 (consistent with screen inputs).

**Cash flow (FY2025, Yahoo fallback):** operating cash flow $3.21bn (+17% vs $2.75bn in FY2024); FCF $2.61bn (+31% vs $2.00bn); dividends paid $718m; share repurchases $3.30bn; net long-term debt issuance $2.13bn. Capital returns exceed FCF, funded by debt markets—consistent with the screen’s leverage failures.

### Interim results (10-Q)

Seven interim 10-Q filings are indexed (Q2 2024 through Q2 2026), all with body extracts. Income-statement tables are present in older quarters (e.g. Q2 2024) but **truncated in the Q2 2026 extract**; interim analysis therefore blends filing MD&A with Yahoo for Q2 2026 totals where noted.

**Q2 2026 (10-Q filed 3 Aug 2026 — primary filing data):**

- Consolidated pretax income: **$1,044m** vs $1,054m in Q2 2025 (−1%); H1 pretax **$1,902m** vs $1,818m (+5%).
- Net fee revenues: Q2 $1,547m (+13%); H1 $2,945m (+12%).
- Gross fee revenues: Q2 $1,578m (+13%); H1 $3,011m (+13%).
- Franchise fees: Q2 $1,023m (+19%); H1 $1,895m (+18%), driven by credit-card fees and RevPAR/rooms growth.
- Worldwide RevPAR: Q2 +3.4% (ADR +3.5%); H1 +3.8% (ADR +3.3%). U.S. & Canada RevPAR Q2 +5.0%, H1 +4.6%. Middle East & Africa weak.
- G&A/other expense: litigation accrual **$27m** in Q2 and H1 2026.
- System size: 10,082 properties, 1,813,698 rooms at 30 Jun 2026 vs 9,805 / 1,779,936 at year-end 2025.
- Liquidity: cash and restricted cash **$472m**; net OCF H1 2026 **$1,806m**; share repurchases H1 **$1,819m**; dividends **$370m**; net debt issuance **$670m**; current ratio 0.5:1.0; credit-facility leverage covenant (Adjusted Total Debt/EBITDA ≤4.5x) **currently satisfied**.

**Q2 2026 totals (Yahoo fallback — income statement absent from filing extract):** total revenue ~$6.65bn; net income ~$648m; diluted EPS $2.43 vs Yahoo Q2 2025 ~$728m / $2.67 (−11% net income year-on-year despite fee growth, reflecting higher interest, litigation, and mix effects).

**Q2 2025 (10-Q, filed 5 Aug 2025):** worldwide RevPAR Q2 +1.5%, H1 +2.8%; net fee revenues H1 $2,618m (+5%); pretax H1 $1,818m.

**Trend summary:** Fee revenue and RevPAR are accelerating into H1 2026, but reported net income growth lags due to financing costs, litigation, and owned/leased segment pressure. The asset-light core is performing; capital structure and one-offs compress bottom-line comparability.

**Gap note:** Ten 8-K filings are indexed; only the August 2025 debt-offering 8-K has a body extract ($1.5bn notes: $400m 4.200% 2027, $500m 4.500% 2031, $600m 5.250% 2035). Other 8-K bodies are missing from the source pack.

risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical exposure.** Hospitality demand is tied to macro travel, corporate budgets, and geopolitical disruption. Management explicitly flags Middle East conflict impacts (Q2 2026 10-Q cautionary statement). RevPAR can decelerate quickly in downturns despite the asset-light model.

**Leverage and liquidity.** Total debt ~$17bn (FY2025); H1 2026 net debt issuance $670m alongside $1.82bn of buybacks. Current ratio 0.5:1.0; working capital structurally negative. The company relies on a $4.5bn revolver and commercial-paper markets; filing states covenants are met and liquidity is adequate for 12+ months, but this is **not** a fortress balance sheet. No going-concern language appears in available extracts.

**Litigation and regulatory.** Ongoing Starwood data-security incident (since 2018): company “unable to reasonably estimate” financial impact (Q2 2026 10-Q). Property-related litigation accrual of $27m in Q2/H1 2026. Legal proceedings referenced under Note 5; EPA settlement discussions noted in Q3 2025 10-Q. These are material overhangs not fully quantified in filings.

**Accounting / capital allocation.** Negative book equity from aggressive repurchases ($27.9bn treasury stock) obscures economic value but signals capital return prioritised over deleveraging. Screen fails financial-health and leverage models; Piotroski “leverage declining” component failed.

**Competitive.** Hilton, IHG, and regional chains compete for owners and loyalty members; citizenM brand acquisition ($349m in 2025 per Q3 2025 10-Q) shows ongoing consolidation costs.

**Customer / franchise concentration.** Not prominently disclosed in available extracts; franchisee health in downturns is an indirect credit risk via fee collections and pipeline conversions.

RiskTags: cyclical, leverage, liquidity, litigation, competitive, accounting

research_rationale: Deep research confirms a high-quality, fee-compounding franchise with solid H1 2026 operating trends and screen-backed quality signals, but elevated leverage, full valuation, and litigation/cyclical risks prevent a stronger endorsement of the quantitative buy signal for strict value mandates.
